title: Reading a big map: layout, labels, search, selection, edge kinds and type shapes
summary: Hub clusters packed by size round the core so Fit shows the whole map about twice as close, with every cluster named; labels placed by priority with no collisions and never under 11 px; a search that counts, lists by type, steps and flies to a match; a selection that lights one hop and frames what it lit when it came from elsewhere; edge kinds told apart by line and end mark, a dash only for proposed; types told apart by silhouette and glyph. The two persona nodes are archetypes for the scenarios, not something to build.

add.label: search-model.js
add.desc: Pure: what a search reads (label, id, file, type, finer kind), how it ranks, the groups by type, the count and the step to the next match.

add.label: search.js
add.desc: The search field's count, its list of matches grouped by type, stepping with Enter, the arrows and N / P, Frame all, and the no-match words.

add.label: glyphs.js
add.desc: The built-in glyph per node type, drawn in the node's core through the same path as theme.icons, and the silhouette per family.

add.label: Maintainer
add.desc: An archetype: the one maintainer who reads the map and decides specs, at a desk or on a phone. Never a real person.

add.label: Household reader
add.desc: An archetype: someone who looks at the map to see what is there and never reviews a spec. Never a real person.

set.desc: Where every node sits: the root and the data core in the middle, then each hub's cluster, largest first, at the free place nearest the centre, 70 px apart; deterministic, no physics.

change.why: every cluster on one ring leaves 84.7% of the box empty, and Fit is zoom 0.057 at 1440 (#218)

set.desc: Pointer and touch on the map, where a click or tap on a cluster's title frames that cluster.

change.why: at Fit a node is 2 px across, so the cluster titles are what a first click can reach (#218)

set.desc: The label overlay: every visible node is a candidate at every zoom, placed greedily in a fixed priority order (selection, matches, lit neighbours, marks, hubs, the rest) with no two labels touching and none under 11 px; a node with no label shows it on hover and focus.

change.why: 296 of 297 nodes go unlabelled at zoom 0.5, and labels are 4 px at the first view (#172)

set.desc: The scene: the focus is one hop over every edge kind (children's lines on request), a dash means only proposed, usage lines are dotted, a cloud call's when is ticks, each edge family has its end mark, and lit edges carry their kind word.

change.why: selecting a hub lights most of the map (#174), and edge kinds differ by colour alone (#176)

set.desc: The Layers menu, and its Key: each edge row drawn with its real line and end mark, one meaning per line style.

change.why: the legend says both Dashed: proposed and Dashed: breaks at the next deploy (#176)

set.desc: The map's tokens, adding --corn-map-label-min and --corn-map-glyph to the font, edge width and glow tokens of the small fixes.

change.why: a theme can set the label floor and the glyph colour, never the meaning of a line (#177)

set.desc: The node panel: the lit lines by kind with counts, Include its children's lines, and what is off screen with Frame them.

change.why: a selection's neighbours stay off screen (#174)

scenarios.title: The maintainer arrives cold and sees the whole map with every big cluster named

steps.text: The clusters are packed by size round the core: on the fixture the box is 5,838 px across, not 13,289.
Fit is zoom 0.128 at 1440, and the cluster titles are drawn at 13 px, the largest first.
A click on a title frames that cluster, where its nodes can be read.

scenarios.title: The maintainer finds a node by name on a map of 900 nodes

steps.text: The maintainer types four letters. The field says 1 of 33 and the list opens, grouped by type.
The matches are ranked: labels that start with the term first, then words, then files, then types and kinds.
Every match wins a label at 11 px or more; nothing else collides with it.
Enter steps to the next match and the camera flies to it at zoom 1.

scenarios.title: The maintainer selects a service and reads what it touches without colour

steps.text: Selecting it lights one hop: what it calls, reads and writes, and its parent.
The panel says Calls 3, Reads 2, and 3 off screen; Frame them brings them in.
Each lit line says its kind in words; a dashed one is proposed, and the Key draws the real marks.

scenarios.title: A household reader zooms over a cluster and reads what it holds

steps.text: At zoom 0.5 about a third of the cluster is labelled, not one node in 297.
Pages, tables and outside services differ by shape, so the colours need no legend.
